Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll begin with `README.md`, then inspect both current wake views as required by the visual-evidence skill. I’ll also consult the fish-control bookshelf before proposing the architecture, and will keep the candidate-specific rationale in the requested notes while extracting one reusable, evidence-backed lesson.

The four sampled solvers have identical headline scores, so I’m checking whether their trajectories, diagnostics, and policies are genuinely identical or whether the score masks useful behavioral differences. I’ll anchor the visual comparison to those metrics before touching the candidate.

The sampled set is four exact replicas of the current captured policy. The inherited comparison is more informative: terminal yaw amplification and target-ray-rate feedforward both preserved capture but worsened crossing quality, without changing the broad route. I’m now inspecting the strong reference and the worse target-ray-rate rollout side by side in both visual rows.

This is the structured re-consultation point: the inherited lineage now has at least four completed terminal overlays with no semantic improvement. The bookshelf requirement therefore applies. I’ll use it to choose one compact mechanism—if any—that addresses the evidence, and will record the required transfer/falsification block before editing.

The visual and trace evidence point to one distinct test: keep the successful target-course/yaw-braking signal unchanged, but briefly reduce posterior carrier work when the head itself is closing fast yet has large point-consistent course slip. This is a phase-local, observation-gated CPG allocation mechanism—not a steering-gain edit—and it directly tests whether competing thrust, rather than missing steering magnitude, causes the terminal oscillation. I’m recording that hypothesis and its falsification boundary before editing the policy.

The projection confirms the mechanism is localized and active: it changes only the 222 parent states below `2.25L`, leaves at least 85% of posterior carrier authority, and does not alter the broad route. Julia is not installed in this worker shell, so I’ll rely on the required pinned checker for contract validation and will repair any static/schema/equivariance issue it reports.

The visual-evidence and bookshelf skills have now shaped the edit: the steering loop is preserved because four terminal steering overlays regressed, while the new mechanism transfers the shelf’s sensor-modulated-rhythm invariant into bounded posterior carrier relief. I’m invoking the required no-CFD checker now.

The pinned checker could not start because its configured model is unavailable in this account, so I’m executing the exact checks from its manifest directly. The guidance and boundary checks are independent of Julia; I’ll also search for a workspace-local Julia executable before treating the runtime check as unavailable.

The boundary check passes. The guidance checker is failing before it examines our lesson because the rendered `README.md` contains the same copied-parent marker twice; that file is outside the allowed edit surface. I’m verifying the checker logic and will use an equivalent parent comparison if this is strictly an upstream duplicate-marker defect.

The candidate now preserves all demonstrated steering and safety layers and changes only posterior carrier authority under measured terminal head slip. I found no undeclared or unused policy parameter, and the solver boundary remains clean; I’m doing the final post-edit boundary/materiality pass and checking the reflection/finite-fallback logic around the new observation path.

The deliverables are complete: one localized carrier-relief candidate, pre-edit/post-edit provenance notes with the required bookshelf transfer block, and a materially revised reusable lesson covering all four failed terminal steering overlays. Boundary, parameter-schema, contract-shape, forbidden-state, and explicit parent-materiality checks pass; no CFD was run.

Produced exactly one candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1): adds point-consistent, terminal slip-gated posterior carrier relief while preserving steering and safety layers.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1): contains visual diagnosis, bookshelf transfer block, hypothesis, falsification, and gate audit.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:215): materially records the four terminal-steering regressions and reusable control implication.

Boundary, schema, static contract, and explicit parent-materiality checks pass. The pinned checker model and Julia executable were unavailable; the rendered README also contains a duplicated parent marker, so those wrapper-level checks could not run unchanged. No CFD was run.
